findings.problem: Article36(b) requires both timely filing and payment of the tax declared. The personal Guide states only timely filing. The other two penalty summaries omit this scoped exception.
findings.fix: Say: If the return and the declared tax were both filed/paid on time and the later difference is no more than JOD5,000, the late charge on the difference runs from notification of the audit decision; above that, art.36(a) applies. Keep the currentness hold. Make the other summaries carry or explicitly cross-reference these conditions.

findings.problem: Imported-service timing loses both partial-payment/service triggers and their proportional limits.
findings.fix: State one month from paying the service fee or any part, to the extent relating to that part; customs release of the item carrying the service; or six months from receiving the service or any part, to the extent relating to that part, whichever applies first. Preserve Director-approved deferral and currentness hold.

findings.problem: Overview says foreign income is taxed only when funded from Jordan, omitting art.3(c)(2) foreign-branch income. Its social-security headline omits ordinary full-coverage scope, and1% monthly interest omits the art.19(a)(2)60-day-from-employment condition.
findings.fix: Include the foreign-branch route with audited final statements, or expressly limit the sentence to resident individuals. Put ordinary full-coverage employment beside14.25%/7.5%. Add the60-day source condition and distinguish source-baseline interest from a current assessment.

findings.problem: Interest/deposit withholding rows omit the taxable-income qualification and domestic bank/financial-company payer condition; corporate row also omits interbank and designated-recipient exceptions. These are explicit neighbors in art.12(a)(2).
findings.fix: Restrict the rows to taxable interest/commissions/qualifying deposit profits paid by banks and financial companies in Jordan; carry the interbank and executive-instruction exclusions beside the corporate figure or state that entitlement remains held until the full exclusion check is made. Preserve finality distinctions.

findings.problem: Some GST positive legal extracts exceed the actually readable evidence: special tax computed first has no supporting clause here; no input in the exempt row is not proved by a schedule-list title; purchases/imports and pre-registration deduction clauses are truncated. The Guide asserts deduction art.19 and refund art.20(d) although the author ledger explicitly says these article numbers were not established.
findings.fix: Read and quote complete official clauses and establish the article numbers, or move the unsupported portion/number to an explicit hold. Retain the readable sales-return and bad-debt material, and the50-500 nonresident departure refund amounts as conditional clause extracts with an article-number hold. Do not clear positive input entitlement using damaged OCR.

findings.problem: National-contribution cessation in art.11(g) applies to all art.11(f), but only the other-companies row states it. The half-year advance due-date row omits the express executive-instruction longer-period exception.
findings.fix: Use a common note beside all national-contribution rows/headline stating art.11(g) applies to every rate and its actual trigger is not cleared. Add unless executive instructions allow a longer period to the advance deadline.

findings.problem: The author ledger is not yet a complete figure ledger: several legal rows use NONE; some multi-rule rows cite only an unrelated clause, and payroll Regulation45 source rowC039 cites IncomeTax art.3. Arithmetic/source-read rows are mixed with legal holdings.
findings.fix: Replace heuristic mappings with all the actual relevant source/quote IDs for each legal proposition, including operative source-baseline conditions. At minimum repair incomeC021/C026/C030/C031/C033; corporateC020/C023/C026/C029/C032; payrollC002/C010-C012/C023/C025/C029/C039; overviewC002/C005-C008/C012/C016; GSTC002/C004/C008/C009/C012-C015/C033. A source table/header/investigation prompt may remain NONE; an assertion of legal entitlement/rate cannot. Add source records for forms, TP, Regulation45 and the fresh MOIN failed-check research.

jo-income-tax.before: If the return was on time and a later difference is up to JOD 5,000, the charge runs from the audit notice (art. 36(b)).
jo-income-tax.after: If both the return and payment of the declared tax were on time and a later tax difference is no more than JOD 5,000, the late charge on that difference starts at notification of the audit decision. Above JOD 5,000, art. 36(a) applies (art. 36(b)).

jo-income-tax.after: | Taxable deposit interest, commissions and qualifying deposit investment profits paid by banks/financial companies in Jordan to an individual | 5% withheld, final | Art. 12(a)(2); interbank deposit interest/profits/commissions and interest/profits for recipients designated by executive instructions are excluded; complete the exclusion check before applying | https://www.moin.gov.jo/ebv4.0/root_storage/ar/eb_list_page/%D9%82%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%88%D9%86_%D8%B6%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A8%D8%A9_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AF%D8%AE%D9%84_%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85_34_%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9_2014_%D9%88%D8%AA%D8%B9%D8%AF%D9%8A%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AA%D9%87.pdf |

jo-corporate-income-tax.before: Failure to withhold makes the payer liable as for its own tax from the remittance date (art. 12(e)).
jo-corporate-income-tax.after: The art. 36(b) exception requires both timely filing and timely payment of the declared tax, followed by a difference no more than JOD 5,000; its charge starts at audit-decision notification. Above that amount art. 36(a) applies. Failure to withhold makes the payer liable as for its own tax from the remittance date (art. 12(e)).

jo-corporate-income-tax.after: Within 30 days of the end of each half year unless executive instructions allow a longer period, art. 19(b)

jordan-gst.before: Input recovery requires a separate art. 19/Schedule 4 check and is not automatically equal to the liability. Pay at the earliest of one month from paying the fee, customs release of the item carrying the service, or six months from receiving the service; the Director may let a registered importer defer.
jordan-gst.after: Input recovery and the exact deduction article number remain on hold; recovery is not automatically equal to the liability. The readable payment clause uses the earliest applicable trigger: one month from payment of the service fee or any part, to the extent relating to that part; customs release of the item carrying the service; or six months from receiving the service or any part, to the extent relating to that part. A registered importer can defer only with the Director’s approval under the executive-instruction conditions. This remains a conditional source extract, not a current payment instruction.

jordan-gst.before: Refuse and refer: Aqaba Special Economic Zone operations (ISTD has a separate Aqaba return), and alcohol, tobacco, fuel or other Special Sales Tax goods, where the special tax is computed first.
jordan-gst.after: Refuse and refer: Aqaba Special Economic Zone operations and any transaction requiring Special Sales Tax classification or a combined computation. The form-list reading shows separate Aqaba returns. The old alcohol/tobacco/fuel classification and claim that special tax is computed first remain explicitly on hold pending the complete schedules and valuation clause.

jordan-gst.before: | Exempt | No GST, no input | Schedule 3, art. 7(b) |
jordan-gst.after: | Exempt | Exempt sale under the readable exemption clause; input treatment is on hold | Schedule 3 list title / art. 7(b) extract; no input entitlement or prohibition inferred from the title |

jordan-gst.before: Non-resident's goods held on departure; these are refund amounts, not purchase-value thresholds, art. 20(d) extract
jordan-gst.after: Non-resident's goods held on departure; these are refund amounts, not purchase-value thresholds. The exact refund article/subparagraph number remains on hold

jordan-gst.before: The art. 19 extract permits deductions for sales returns, qualifying bad debts, business purchases/imports other than Schedule 4, and eligible pre-registration stock, subject to the detailed conditions. The Schedule 4 contents and apportionment rules are on hold; do not allow input tax solely because a payment appears in a bank statement.
jordan-gst.after: The readable deduction fragments cover tax previously accounted for or paid on returned sales and general tax on deferred-payment sales that became bad debts. The purchases/imports and pre-registration-stock subclauses are truncated, so those positive entitlements, the exact deduction article number, blocked-input schedule and apportionment instructions remain explicitly on hold. Do not allow input tax solely because a payment appears in a bank statement.

jordan-gst.before: Original examples/test cases using those assumptions remain held.
jordan-gst.after: Original examples/test cases using those assumptions remain held. Additional explicit evidence holds: special-tax-first valuation, input treatment of exempt supplies, purchases/imports and pre-registration-stock deduction entitlement, and exact deduction/refund article and subparagraph numbers. The readable returned-sale, bad-debt and departure-refund fragments do not close those holds.

jo-tax-overview.before: a resident's foreign income is taxed only where it arises from funds or deposits from Jordan (art. 3).
jo-tax-overview.after: art. 3(c) separately covers a resident’s net foreign income arising from funds or deposits from Jordan, and net income of a Jordanian company’s foreign branch declared in final financial statements certified by an external public accountant. Neither route replaces the other.
| Social security | Ordinary employment covered by all four insurances: employer 14.25%, employee 7.5%; exclusions and reductions require the detailed coverage check |

jo-tax-overview.before: Late income tax and GST payment costs 0.4% per week or part of a week. Contributions carry 1% a month.
jo-tax-overview.after: The source baseline states 0.4% per week or part for late income tax and GST. The income-tax art. 36(b) exception requires both timely return and timely payment of declared tax, with a later difference no more than JOD 5,000; its charge starts at audit-decision notification, while larger differences follow art. 36(a). For SSC the source states 1% monthly, with interest accruing after 60 days from employment under art. 19(a)(2). All these statements remain under the relevant currentness hold and do not determine a current assessment.

jo-tax-overview.after: 1% to 7% for companies; 1% above JOD 200,000 for individuals; art. 11(g) cessation applies to every rate, and occurrence of its debt-ratio trigger is not cleared

Held unsupported special-tax-first valuation, exempt input treatment, purchases/imports/pre-registration positive deduction entitlement and exact deduction/refund article numbers. Retained only readable returned-sale/bad-debt and50-500tax-refund fragments.
Cessation condition now appears beside each national-contribution rate and overview headline; half-year-advance timing states executive-instruction longer-period exception.

Added forms,TP,Regulation45,MOIN source records;218historical rows and initial review receipts unchanged.
